LESSON: PROHIBITIONS IN ISLAM • INCEST • BESTIALITY • PROSTITUTION • HOMOSEXUALITY

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: Akhlaq (Moral Teachings)
Topic 5.3: Prohibitions in Islam • Incest • Bestiality • Prostitution • Homosexuality
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 16

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Prohibitions in Islam • Incest • Bestiality • Prostitution • Homosexuality, part of Akhlaq (Moral Teachings) in Grade 8 ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION.

Key inquiry question: What causes deviant sexual behaviour in the society? 2. What is the rationale for the prohibition of deviant sexual behaviour in Islam?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. explain the causes of deviant sexual behaviour to safeguard oneself,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Prohibitions in Islam • Incest • Bestiality • Prostitution • Homosexuality in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. describe the effects of deviant sexual behaviour in the society,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Prohibitions in Islam • Incest • Bestiality • Prostitution • Homosexuality in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. explain the rationale for the prohibition of deviant sexual behaviour in Islam,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Prohibitions in Islam • Incest • Bestiality • Prostitution • Homosexuality in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. appreciate the rationale for the prohibition of deviant sexual behaviour.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Prohibitions in Islam • Incest • Bestiality • Prostitution • Homosexuality in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. explain the causes of deviant sexual behaviour to safeguard oneself,

   Prohibitions in Islam • Incest • Bestiality • Prostitution • Homosexuality helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. describe the effects of deviant sexual behaviour in the society,

   Prohibitions in Islam • Incest • Bestiality • Prostitution • Homosexuality helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. explain the rationale for the prohibition of deviant sexual behaviour in Islam,

   Prohibitions in Islam • Incest • Bestiality • Prostitution • Homosexuality helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. appreciate the rationale for the prohibition of deviant sexual behaviour.

   Prohibitions in Islam • Incest • Bestiality • Prostitution • Homosexuality helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. identify deviant sexual behaviour (incest, bestiality, prostitution, and homosexuality) and make notes,

2. research on the causes of deviant sexual behaviour (incest, bestiality, prostitution, and homosexuality) and make notes,

3. discuss the effects of deviant sexual behaviour (incest, bestiality, prostitution, and homosexuality) in the society in groups and present on charts/PowerPoint,

4. watch video clips on the effects of deviant sexual behaviour (incest, bestiality, prostitution, and homosexuality) and make notes,

5. listen to a resource person explaining the causes, effects 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. identify deviant sexual behaviour (incest, bestiality, prostitution, and homosexuality) and make notes,
2. research on the causes of deviant sexual behaviour (incest, bestiality, prostitution, and homosexuality) and make notes,
3. discuss the effects of deviant sexual behaviour (incest, bestiality, prostitution, and homosexuality) in the society in groups and present on charts/PowerPoint,
4. watch video clips on the effects of deviant sexual behaviour (incest, bestiality, prostitution, and homosexuality) and make notes,
5. listen to a resource person explaining the causes, effects 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Prohibitions in Islam • Incest • Bestiality • Prostitution • Homosexuality together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Self-efficacy: the skill of effective communication enhanced as learners discuss the effects of deviant sexual

behaviour in the society in groups, and present on charts/PowerPoint.

• Communication and collaboration: teamwork is enhanced as learners contribute to the discussion on the effects

of deviant sexual behaviour in the society.

• Learning to learn: the skill of research enhanced as learners research on the causes of deviant sexual behaviour

and make notes.

Values:
Responsibility is enhanced as learners research on the rationale for the prohibition of deviant sexual behaviour.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Awareness on health-related issues such as HIV and AIDS is enhanced as learners discuss the effects of deviant sexual

behaviour in the society.

Link to other subjects

Social studies and Life Skills Education as learners discuss the effects of deviant sexual behaviour in the society.
